label: Irregular Verbs
outcome: Lo studente recupera rapidamente le forme irregolari ad alta frequenza, usa la forma di Past Simple in un contesto passato e il past participle dopo un ausiliare, e distingue le due forme senza affidarsi a una lista alfabetica.
must_master: choose Past Simple form versus past participle from grammatical context
retrieve forms inside meaningful sentences rather than only from infinitive-to-form tables
recognise useful form families and recurring patterns without treating them as exception-free rules

scope_boundary.present_perfect: Use have/has + past participle only as a clear grammatical signal for the participle form. Do not teach Present Perfect meanings, time adverbs or Past Simple vs Present Perfect choice yet.
scope_boundary.verb_inventory: Prioritise a compact high-frequency core rather than an exhaustive school list. Less frequent verbs can be added later through SRS or programme-specific practice.
scope_boundary.pronunciation: Do not turn this Recovery topic into a pronunciation course, but flag read/read/read as a spelling trap if used.
scope_boundary.regional_variants: Avoid grading dialect-sensitive participles unless all standard variants are accepted.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using the Past Simple form after have/has
using the participle as the simple past
memorising isolated triples but failing to retrieve the form in a sentence
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: knowing go-went-gone but writing I go there yesterday
italian_learner_risks.target: retrieve went from the finished-past context

italian_learner_risks.risk: assuming every irregular verb follows the same vowel-change pattern
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: creating forms by analogy rather than retrieving the stored form
italian_learner_risks.target: use pattern families as memory support, not grammar rules

context_bank: a weekend or school trip recap
what someone ate, drank, bought or took
messages about people someone saw or met
a short sequence of completed actions
a checklist of things someone has or has not done, used only to cue the participle form
choosing between a Past Simple form and a participle from the surrounding auxiliary

include one Italian-to-English contextual translation

quality_rejections: an alphabetical wall of 40-100 verb triples
a lesson made only of base → past → participle table completion
teaching Present Perfect meaning before the dedicated topic
testing rare verbs while high-frequency forms remain uncovered
treating form families as exception-free transformation rules
using dialect-sensitive forms without accepting standard variants
more than two consecutive items with no sentence-level context
difficulty created by obscure vocabulary rather than verb-form retrieval
